payload.markdown: When I described class type declarations, I implied that types and classes are synonymous. There is a key difference between the two, however. When you define a class, you also define a type, but a type can describe an entire family of classes. The mechanism by which different classes can be grouped together under a type is called inheritance. I discuss inheritance in the next section.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Inheritance: Deriving a class from a base class to reuse and specialise its behaviour.
Nullable Types: Types that explicitly allow null, written as ?
Type Declarations: Parameter and return types that constrain what a function accepts and returns.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Null Safe Operator: ?-> short-circuits an entire chain when the receiver is null.
Primitive Types: int, float, string and bool: PHP's scalar building blocks.
